chunks: Our father and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may God be pleased with them) narrated, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from some of his companions, from Ahmad ibn Umar al-Halabi, from Abu Basir, who said: I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and said to him: The Shiites say that the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) taught Ali (peace be upon him) a gate from which a thousand gates are opened, each gate opening a thousand gates.

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: O Abu Muhammad! I swear by God that the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) taught Ali (peace be upon him) a thousand gates, each gate opening a thousand gates. I said to him: By God, this is true knowledge! He said: Indeed, it is knowledge, and for no one else but him, and it is not that (i.e., not exclusive in a way that implies exclusivity of the concept, but rather specific to Ali's station).

key_terms.وَلِأَحَدٍ غَيْرِهِ: And for no one else (indicating exclusivity)
key_terms.يَفْتَحُ: Opens (metaphorically for revealing deeper layers of knowledge)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the 'thousand gates of knowledge' taught to Imam Ali in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Khisal*, Imam al-Sadiq confirms the Shi'a belief in the unique, hierarchical transmission of divine knowledge (*'Ilm*) to Imam Ali, validating the concept of 'one thousand gates, each opening to a thousand.' This hadith serves as a key proof for the doctrine of the Imam's comprehensive knowledge, distinguishing the Ahl al-Bayt's spiritual inheritance from the general scholarly knowledge possessed by others. It underscores the Shia view that while others may possess fragments of wisdom, the complete, structured cosmic knowledge was exclusively granted to the Imams.
